feedback_request.integration_feedback: Report whether line_loss_events stayed at 0 with the ±0.05 span. Report max_error on each track and whether it moved from the 0.061 floor. Say whether slalom progress recovered compared with 0.035 at ±0.06. Say whether the wheel_radius 0.035 change made the robot faster or changed steering_oscillation, and whether the outer sensors at ±0.05 saturate on slalom. Note any controller change you needed for the new radius and speed.

intent: Test two geometry levers at once, with per-track metrics separating their effects. Narrow the outer sensor span from ±0.06 m to ±0.05 m to recover slalom progress while keeping the line covered out to about 0.07 m of lateral error. Raise wheel_radius from 0.03 to 0.035 m to add turn authority and test whether the max_error floor near 0.061 m moves. Keep wheel_track at 0.12 m, y = 0.03, the 16 mm footprint, the 0.8 kg mass and the body fixed. Expected: no line losses, slalom progress above 0.06, and max_error on oval and s-bend below about 0.058.
learning: Iterations 0 to 3 show that max_error is pinned at about 0.061 regardless of sensor span (±0.04 vs ±0.06), footprint, lookahead, or wheel_track (0.10 vs 0.12). Sensing gaps are ruled out by the line-loss fix. wheel_track is ruled out as a lever. The remaining geometry levers are wheel_radius, mass and sensor footprint. Slalom progress is sensitive to span: ±0.04 gave 0.110 with line losses and ±0.06 gave 0.035 without them, so the best span may lie between. If this race shows that max_error moves with wheel_radius, keep the radius and tune span. If it does not, test mass next.
rationale: The evidence from iterations 0 to 3 points to a geometry limit that the span and track changes have not moved. Max_error sits at 0.0609 to 0.0618 on every track in every design, just past the 0.06 m off-track floor. Oval progress is 0.115 in all designs, so the failure point does not depend on the sensing changes. Iteration 3 changed wheel_track from 0.10 to 0.12 m, and its metrics match iteration 2 to four decimal places. That means wheel_track had no measurable effect, so the mismatch-drift hypothesis for wheel_track is not supported. The Integrator's own rule says that if max_error stays near 0.061 with wheel_track 0.12, I should change wheel_radius to 0.035. That condition is met. Slalom progress fell from 0.105 (±0.04 span, line losses) to 0.035 (±0.06 span, no line losses). The Integrator's rule says that if slalom progress stays below about 0.06 with the ±0.06 span, I should move the outer sensors to ±0.05. That condition is also met. The ±0.06 span removed line losses, but a coverage-edge estimate (about 0.048 m reach plus half the tape width) suggests ±0.05 with 16 mm footprints still reaches about 0.07 m of lateral error, so line losses should stay at 0. I therefore change two things: outer sensors to ±0.05 and wheel_radius to 0.035. Because the metrics are reported per track, the slalom result mainly tests the span and the oval and s-bend results mainly test the radius. I keep y = 0.03, the 16 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.12, mass 0.8 and body fixed. Expected: line_loss_events stay at 0, slalom progress rises above 0.06, and max_error on oval and s-bend moves measurably from 0.061. If max_error does not move with the larger radius, the floor is not a geometry-driven limit and the next lever is mass or sensor footprint.
